# A nested Effect run turns dependency tracking back on mid-pause

## Context

A downstream whitebox e2e hung its App Worker after one store reconfiguration. The Neural Link call returned in 115 ms, and every later call timed out. CDP `Debugger.pause` samples of the SharedWorker, taken 3, 5 and 7 s later, all sat inside the store's rebuild. Each rebuild ran from the same frames: a `Base` construct callback (`me.isReady = true`, `src/core/Base.mjs:320`) ended its config batch (`src/Neo.mjs:494`), and `EffectManager.resume()` ran the store's rebuild Effect again.

That Effect does its work between `EffectManager.pauseTracking()` and `resumeTracking()`. Its work fires an event whose listeners create components, and creating components runs Effects.

Engine-only repro (Node, `dev` at `f82061f2c9`):

```js
new Effect(() => {
    runs++;
    probe.tracked;                 // the intended dependency

    EffectManager.pauseTracking();
    try {
        new Effect(() => {});      // any nested Effect run
        probe.untracked;           // must stay untracked
    } finally {
        EffectManager.resumeTracking()
    }
});

probe.untracked = 2;               // runs === 2; expected 1
```

With a nesting-safe counter patched into `EffectManager`, the same script gives 1. `probe.tracked = 2` still re-runs the Effect, and the counter ends at 0.

## The Problem

`pauseTracking()` sets `isTrackingPaused = true`, and `resumeTracking()` sets it back to `false`. `Effect.run()` brackets its own `isRunning` reads and writes with exactly these calls (`src/core/Effect.mjs:123-125`, `:138-140`, `:155-157`). So the first Effect that runs inside an outer untracked region ends that region. Everything the outer code reads afterwards becomes a dependency of the active effect.

An Effect that depends on reads it meant to skip re-runs on unrelated writes. If its own work causes those writes later, for example instances it creates flipping `isReady`, it never settles. That is the hang above: each rebuild creates columns, each column's `isReady` re-runs the rebuild.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/core/EffectManager.mjs:20, 75-77, 126-128`: the boolean. The batching `pause()`/`resume()` beside it is a counter.
- Callers relying on an untracked region:
  - `src/state/Provider.mjs:483-490`: a binding effect writes `component[configKey]` with tracking paused, because "tracking those would re-run the formatter on every unrelated write". A write that ends a batch runs queued effects, and the first of them ends the pause early.
  - `src/functional/useMemo.mjs:77-79`: reads one value, with no nested run. It is unaffected, but becomes correct by construction.
  - Downstream code that rebuilds with tracking paused.
- #7085 introduced the flag for `Effect.run()`'s self-dependency problem. The same ticket replaced the batching boolean with a counter because "the simple boolean flag could not handle nested `pause()`/`resume()` calls, breaking encapsulation".

Design authority: `EffectManager.pauseTracking()`: "Disables dependency tracking for the currently active effect." A pause that any nested run can end does not do that for the outer effect. #7085 set the bar for the sibling: "Robust Nesting: Nested batches or pause calls now work flawlessly."

## The Fix

Make tracking pause nesting-safe and scoped to the effect it was raised for, in `src/core/EffectManager.mjs`:

- A `trackingPauseCounter`. `pauseTracking()` increments it; `resumeTracking()` decrements it, never below 0.
- The counter belongs to the active effect. `push()` saves it and starts the pushed effect at 0, so an effect that runs inside an untracked region still tracks its own reads. `pop()` restores the outer effect's counter.
- `isTrackingPaused` becomes a getter (`trackingPauseCounter > 0`), so existing readers keep working. No engine test writes it.
- Unit arms in `test/playwright/unit/core/Effect.spec.mjs`: the repro above, an effect created inside a pause, and an unmatched resume. The Provider binding arm lives in `test/playwright/unit/state/Provider.spec.mjs`: after a bound write whose afterSet builds an Effect, an unrelated write must not re-run the formatter.

*Amended during implementation:* a global counter alone broke `functional/UseMemo.spec.mjs`'s child-instance arm. The memoized child's own render Effect ran inside the parent's pause and lost its subscriptions. The boolean had kept nested effects tracking only through the same reset that clobbered outer pauses, so the pause belongs to the stack frame.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback / Edge Case | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EffectManager.pauseTracking()` / `resumeTracking()` / `isTrackingPaused` | Their JSDoc; #7085's nesting principle | Pairs nest: tracking resumes only when the outermost pair ends. `isTrackingPaused` stays readable. | An extra `resumeTracking()` clamps at 0 instead of going negative. | JSDoc on all three | Repro arm red on `dev`, green after; Provider arm; existing Effect, EffectBatching and Provider specs; full unit suite |
| `EffectManager.push()` / `pop()` | `pauseTracking()`'s "for the currently active effect" | A pushed effect starts with tracking enabled; `pop()` restores the outer effect's pause. | An unmatched `pop()` restores 0. | JSDoc on both | Effect created inside a pause still subscribes; `UseMemo.spec.mjs` green |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An untracked read after a nested Effect run inside `pauseTracking()` creates no dependency. The arm is red on `dev` and green with the fix.
- [ ] Tracked reads before and after the region still subscribe.
- [ ] An Effect created inside a `pauseTracking()` region still subscribes to its own reads.
- [ ] A Provider binding whose bound write runs an Effect does not subscribe the binding effect to that write's later afterSet reads.
- [ ] `resumeTracking()` without a matching pause cannot drive the counter below 0.
- [ ] `isTrackingPaused` reads correctly; the full unit suite is green.

## Out of Scope

- Which reads an Effect tracks by default, and the batching `pause()`/`resume()`.
- Downstream workarounds; they become unnecessary.

## Avoided Traps

- **Saving and restoring the boolean inside `Effect.run()`:** it repairs that method's own pairs, but any other nested pair still ends an outer pause. A counter covers every pair.
- **A global counter without per-frame scope:** nested effects then inherit the outer pause and stop tracking their own reads (measured: `UseMemo.spec.mjs:154` red).
- **Deferring untracked work to a microtask:** it breaks the synchronous contract of an Effect run at batch end.
